block.createdangerclose.ballistic_comput: _Joins_ that interface's Battle Network, reads its sensors and _sends_ firing solutions to its servos.
Each kind of module _adds a capability_. The computer's goggles list what is installed and what is missing.

block.createdangerclose.correlator.toolt: Rangefinders ranging the _same target_ are _merged_ into one more accurate fix.
When part of a computer's bank:
A module for the _Ballistic Computer_. Combines several rangefinders.
block.createdangerclose.differentiator.t: The guns _lead_ a moving target, and servos _track smoothly_ instead of lagging behind.
When part of a computer's bank:
A module for the _Ballistic Computer_. Works out how fast the target is moving.
block.createdangerclose.fire_mission_con: Shows the _target_, the _trajectory_ and each gun's _firing solution_ through Goggles.

Sets a _fuze correction_ from -40 to +40 ticks (2 seconds), added to timed fuzes: early for an _airburst_ short of the target, late so a base-fuzed _armour-piercing_ shell bursts _inside_ after piercing. On _delayed impact_ and _delayed inertia_ fuzes it sets the delay after impact instead. Scrolling turns it 5 ticks a notch, or 1 with _Shift_ held; _right-click_ the knob to zero it.
_Fires_ every gun that has a solution and is _on target_. The others hold fire.

The gunnery officer's station: shows the _fire mission_ and gives the _orders_.
block.createdangerclose.fuze_computer.to: _Timed fuzes_ in loaded shells are _set_ to the time of flight.
When part of a computer's bank:
A module for the _Ballistic Computer_. Works out fuze times.
block.createdangerclose.integrator.toolt: A rangefinder solution is _held for 10 seconds_ after ranging stops, and the ship's own speed is _compensated_ (needs Velocity Sensors). With a _Differentiator_, the held target keeps moving.
When part of a computer's bank:
A module for the _Ballistic Computer_. Keeps the solution running between readings.

_Opens_ the table, showing all its maps stitched together. _Right-click_ the maps to mark a _target_.
_Shows_ the ship's position and _sends_ the marked target to the _Ballistic Computer_.

block.createdangerclose.navigation_conso: _Shows_ each reading the network has a _sensor_ for: Gimbal, heading, Velocity and Altitude.
When a powered Battle Network Interface faces it:
Shows the ship's own _attitude_, _speed_ and _altitude_ through Goggles.
block.createdangerclose.network_interfac: _Polls_ the sensor at a rate proportional to input RPM.

_Connects_ the table: it shows the ship and the computer's plot, and its target goes to the computer.

createdangerclose.ponder.ballistic_compu: Computing firing solutions with the Ballistic Computer
The Ballistic Computer works out firing solutions for the guns on its Battle Network
Look at the computer with Goggles to see which modules it has, and what is missing
It has no shaft of its own: a Network Interface facing it connects it and drives it
On its own, it can only aim at a fixed point. Modules add the rest
Differentiator: the guns lead moving targets
Correlator: several rangefinders on one target are merged into a better fix
Integrator: the solution is held between readings, and the ship's own speed is corrected for
Fuze Computer: timed fuzes are set to the time of flight
Modules count when they touch the computer, directly or through other modules, in any shape
One of each kind is enough. Two computers must not share modules
createdangerclose.ponder.battle_damage.t: Fire control equipment can be damaged in battle
Right-click with Honeycomb: one click lubricates the whole computer bank, and frees what has seized
A close blast, or a shell or shrapnel passing through, breaks it: it stops working until repaired
A blast further off jostles it: it still works, but throws every aim off a little
Left-click jostled equipment with a Wrench to set it true
Right-click a broken mechanism with a Precision Mechanism
Servos and Network Interfaces break a cog instead
Right-click it with a Cogwheel: either half of a servo will do
Mechanisms dry out over the days, faster the faster their network runs: power down to make it last
Run dry, a working mechanism may seize, and stops
createdangerclose.ponder.cannon_servo.he: Aiming Cannon Mounts with Cannon Servos
createdangerclose.ponder.cannon_servo.te: A Cannon Servo turns one axis of a Cannon Mount for the Ballistic Computer
Its input sits on the Battle Network...
...and its output drives the cannon's own network. The two networks never join
One servo drives the mount's elevation...
...the other its traverse. Each finds out which one it drives on its own
When the computer has a firing solution, the servos train the gun onto it
On target, the servos hold it there, and keep following a moving solution
The cannon may be fired as usual or from the Fire Mission Console
createdangerclose.ponder.fire_mission_co: Giving fire orders with the Fire Mission Console
The Fire Mission Console gives the orders to the guns on its network
Press again within a few seconds to confirm, and it fires
Scroll over the knob on the left to correct timed fuzes: earlier for an airburst, later to burst inside after piercing
Right-click the knob to zero it
Look at the console with Goggles to see the target, the trajectory and each gun's solution
A Network Interface facing it connects it to the Ballistic Computer
The guns train onto the computer's firing solution
Right-click the lever in the middle to switch the trajectory
Plunging fire: shells drop steeply, over cover and onto decks
Direct fire: a flatter, faster path to targets in plain sight
Right-click the button on the right to fire every gun that is on target
Guns still training onto their solution hold their fire, so no shell is wasted
Danger close: if a salvo would land near your own guns, spotters or ships, the first press only warns
createdangerclose.ponder.map_table.heade: Plotting fire missions on a Map Table
createdangerclose.ponder.map_table.text_: Map Tables placed side by side join into one table, up to 3×3
Green: spotters, players out in the field carrying a copy of one of the maps
While connected, the table keeps its maps up to date around itself, as a player holding them would...
...and around each target being ranged. Ground out of loaded range stays as last seen
Right-click it with Filled Maps to lay them out. They must fit together like the land, north up
Right-click with an empty hand to open the table GUI to see and manage its maps
There, right-click the maps to mark a target
On its own, the table only keeps the target as a note
A Network Interface facing it sends the target to the Ballistic Computer...
...and the table shows where the ship is
Red: each gun's reach and where it points. Inside the inner ring is too close to hit
White: where a rangefinder has ranged, in a blue circle of how far off it may be
createdangerclose.ponder.navigation_cons: Reading the ship's motion on a Navigation Console
The Navigation Console shows the ship's attitude, speed and altitude
A Network Interface facing it connects it to the Battle Network
It has no instruments of its own: it shows what the sensors on the network read
A Gimbal Sensor gives the ship's pitch and roll...
Velocity and Altitude Sensors on the network add the ship's speed and height
Look at the console with Goggles to read it, and to see which sensors are missing
createdangerclose.ponder.network_interfa: Connecting sensors to a Battle Network
Fire control equipment shares one kinetic network: the Battle Network
A Network Interface reads the sensor it faces and shares the reading with the network
It needs at least 32 RPM, and polls its sensor more often the faster it turns
Facing a Ballistic Computer, an interface connects the computer to the network and drives it
The computer then works with every sensor on the Battle Network
Interfaces also connect Map Tables, Navigation Consoles and Fire Mission Consoles
createdangerclose.ponder.piped_lubricati: Mechanisms can also be lubricated by pipe: with Spindle Oil, or another mod's lubricating or plant oil
Spindle Oil is pressed from Honeycomb and Water in a heated Basin
Each keeps a small reservoir. Oil piped into any cabinet of a bank, or the interface driving it, lubricates the whole bank
Servos and other interfaces take a pipe of their own
Piping oil into every cabinet is not needed, but keeps the bank supplied if one is lost in battle
createdangerclose.ponder.rangefinder.tex: A Rangefinder Bearing carries a rangefinder tube and trains it
On the Battle Network, its target goes to the Ballistic Computer
Map Tables on the network chart the ground around the aim point
Two Rangefinder Lenses go at the ends of a bar across their line of sight, looking the same way
The further apart they are, the more accurate the range
The Rangefinder Eyepiece bolts onto the back of the tube, centred between the lenses
Glue the tube together with Super Glue
Right-click the bearing to assemble the tube
Right-click the eyepiece to take the seat: the tube follows where you look
It turns faster the faster its network runs
Hold right-click on a target to range it: once the tube is steady, the two markers merge
createdangerclose.ponder.rangefinder_upk: Blasts, shells and shrapnel crack lenses: the range becomes far less accurate
Right-click a cracked lens with a Glass Pane to repair it
Dust settles on lenses over the days, fastest in hot, dry places: the view clouds over and ranging suffers
Rain washes it off, where the lens is open to the sky
Or wipe it clean: right-click it with a Water Bucket
